Big shake-up at DC Studios. Skydance confirmed that James Gunn and Peter Safran are stepping down as co-CEOs starting December 1, 2026, with Jeremy Latcham stepping in as President and Chief Creative Officer.

To keep the facts straight alongside my reaction:
* I said Man of Steel in the clip, but the upcoming Superman film Gunn is writing and directing is officially Man of Tomorrow.
* The upcoming series is officially titled The People v. Gorilla Grodd.
* Per Skydance’s announcement, Gunn and Safran aren’t leaving those projects or The Batman Part II, and are shifting back to full-time creative and producing work.

My frustration is strictly about how fast the corporate messaging changed, and my wondering what happens after their current slate is just my own speculation. Does this change your confidence in the DCU slate?

@dcofficial @jamesgunn 

#DCStudios #JamesGunn #DCU #ManOfTomorrow #FilmNews

James Gunn and Peter Safran are officially OUT as the heads of DC Studios starting December 1st and John Campea was right all along. 

After months of David Ellison insisting that Gunn and Safran were staying put on the post-merger leadership roster, former Marvel executive Jeremy Latcham is suddenly stepping in to run DC. We finally had a unified roadmap for the DCU, and now it feels like history repeating itself with executive interference. 

Full video breakdown dropping soon keep an eye on the page. How are you feeling about this DC shakeup? Let me know in the comments!

Do not skip Clayface just because it looks like a horror movie.

Quick PSA:
It is not scary. If horror movies scare you, do not worry. This one will not scare you. It has a little body horror, but it is not that bad. You can deal with it.
The AMC popcorn buckets and cup are not that great. Not my favorite, but here they are if you want to see them.
This movie is great.
This is a hard R movie. There is a lot of gore, but I still think you will like it a lot, and it is a good way to get introduced to James Gunn's Gotham.
Main point: do not skip this just because it looks like a horror movie. It is not that scary, so definitely consider checking it out.

Stepping behind the curtain of the gaming and creator economy at IGN’s Women in Gaming event earlier this year.  

I got to sit in on the “Power Play: How Brands, Creators & Games Win Together” panel and listen to an incredible lineup of women leading the charge across tech, gaming, and brand partnerships. Hearing insights directly from leaders at Meta, CAA, Best Buy, Roblox, and Open World was a huge reminder of how fast the intersection of gaming and content creation is evolving.  

Just wanted to share a look at some of the industry events I’ve been covering behind the scenes. Plenty more event coverage, reviews, and creator breakdowns on the way stay tuned.

Panelists: Cat Coddington (Meta), Jennifer Erb (CAA), Kirsten Hayhoe (Best Buy), Stephanie Latham (Roblox), & Nadia (Open World).
